title: Average-Based DI
tagline: Year 2 — Averages across rows and columns, comparisons and effects of changes

introduction.overview: Average-based DI sets give a table of marks, sales or other quantities, and ask for averages across rows (per student) and across columns (per subject), for the whole table, and for the effect of changes such as adding a mark. Because an average is a total divided by a count, the easiest approach is to compute row totals and column totals first and then divide when needed.
introduction.placementRelevance: Average-based DI sets are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds and test accuracy in addition and division more than any new concept.
introduction.realWorldContext: Class results, performance reports and monthly summaries are all averaged across rows and columns.

learningObjectives: Compute row and column totals once and reuse them
Compute averages across a row, a column or the whole table
Compare averages and find the highest and lowest
Find the marks needed to reach a target average
Compute percentages and differences from averages

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Average = total ÷ count. Total = average × count. The grand total equals the sum of row totals and also the sum of column totals.

coreDefinitions: Row total: sum of values across a row (one student).
Column total: sum of values down a column (one subject).
Row average: row total ÷ number of columns. Column average: column total ÷ number of rows.
Grand total: sum of all values; overall average = grand total ÷ number of values.
Target average: the average you want to reach; needed total = target × count.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Averages are totals in disguise. If you hold the row totals and column totals, you can answer almost any average question with a single division. The grand total gives a useful check: row totals and column totals must add to the same number.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Add a total column and a total row to the table. Use these totals for all later questions, and check the grand total from both directions.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Row and column averages
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Row avg = row total ÷ 4;  Column avg = column total ÷ 5

mainNarrative: Add a total column and a total row. Student A has 78 + 82 + 74 + 66 = 300, so average 75. Maths has 78 + 85 + 64 + 90 + 72 = 389 over five students, an average of 77.8.
The grand total is the sum of all row totals: 300 + 324 + 282 + 336 + 292 = 1534. Check by summing the column totals: 389 + 385 + 392 + 368 = 1534. The overall average is 1534 ÷ 20 = 76.7.

To find the best student, compare row totals; to find the best subject, compare column totals or averages. Student D has the highest total (336), and Chemistry has the highest average (392 ÷ 5 = 78.4).
For a target average, work with totals. To average 80 in four subjects, a student needs 320. Student A has 300, so would need 20 more marks, which is a rise of 5 in each subject on average.
For relative comparisons, use the average as the base: if the class average in Maths is 77.8, then D's 90 is (90 − 77.8) ÷ 77.8 × 100 = 15.7% above the average.

deepDiveAspects.title: Average of averages
deepDiveAspects.content: Because every row has the same number of cells, the average of the row averages equals the overall average. With unequal counts this fails.

deepDiveAspects.title: Effect of a change
deepDiveAspects.content: If one mark changes by d, the row total changes by d and the row average by d ÷ 4, the column average by d ÷ 5 and the overall average by d ÷ 20.

solvedExamples.title: Row average
solvedExamples.question: Find the average marks of student A.

solvedExamples.title: Column average
solvedExamples.question: Find the average marks in Maths for the five students.

solvedExamples.title: Target average
solvedExamples.question: How many more marks in total does student A need to reach an average of 80 in the four subjects?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Averages are totals divided by the count.

shortcutMethods.title: Totals first

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Add a total row and a total column. Use them for every question and check the grand total from both directions.

rulesForApplication: Average is the base for percentages.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Using the value as the base.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: An average must lie between the smallest and largest values in its row or column.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The grand total check catches most errors.
